newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-STRANG VIEWS KENT CONTRACT AS KEY CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-STRANG VIEWS KENT CONTRACT AS KEY CHALLENGE.

text.p: Zimbabwe leg-spinner Paul Strang, signed up as Kent's overseas player for the forthcoming season, believes his game will benefit greatly from learning to adapt to English wickets.

The 26-year-old Strang, signed by the county last Friday to replace West Indian all-rounder Carl Hooper, is also viewing the 1997 English county championship as a significant challenge in his rapidly developing career.

"I've made no secret of the fact that I'd like to play county cricket in England -- I think it can develop my game and I consider it as an important challenge for me as a leg-spinner who's still got a hell of a lot to learn," Strang told Reuters.

"Obviously you can't bowl on what you like all the time so I also consider that half the challenge: learning to adapt to conditions. The last few summers in England, I believe, have been quite dry and the wickets have started to break up and turn later on.
"It's four-day cricket over there as well so, on the fourth day, a lot happens. I've got no worries about the wickets."
Although Strang is unsure of the exact make-up of the Kent side he will be joining, he is expecting to play for a well-supported county with an aggressive approach to the game.

"I remember, when Kent came out to Zimbabwe on a pre-season tour a few years ago, they were quite a young bunch. They had a lot of pretty aggressive batsmen ready to go out and take the bull by the horns -- and I presume they're much the same now.
"I'd just like to get in there for Kent, bowl and get some wickets and contribute some useful lower order runs."
Strang's test career is still in its infancy but he has enjoyed a golden spell over the past six months.

In 13 tests to date, he has so far taken 32 wickets at an average of 39.93. He has captured three five-wicket hauls against Pakistan, Sri Lanka and England respectively, with a best return of 5-106 against Sri Lanka in Colombo last year.

He has also been a dependable and gutsy lower order batsman for Zimbabwe at test level, having compiled 505 runs at an impressive average of 31.56. His highest score is 106 not out -- achieved against Pakistan in Sheikhupura.

Strang, who is also a brilliant out-fielder, feels Kent is the right county for him. "Chatting to the secretary of the club, I believe they're a nice bunch of guys with a good changing-room spirit. It's a very well-supported club and that's what you need. I think, if you want to go over there, you've got to do it properly -- and, for me, Kent's a great place to go."
Strang will join his new county on April 18 after Zimbabwe have competed with Pakistan and Sri Lanka in the Sharjah one-day tournament.
